rules.quote: Write clear page titles. This is the first thing a screen reader user will hear and should align with the first heading on the page.
rules.violation_condition: a page title that does not align with the first heading (H1) on the page
rules.why: G-4: actionable sentence instructing alignment between page title and first heading.

rules.quote: Don’t rely on colour alone to structure pages.
rules.violation_condition: conveying page structure or information solely through colour
rules.why: Clear negative instruction from accessibility requirements.

rules.quote: Don’t rely on sensory characteristics such as shape, size, visual location, orientation or sound to explain things.
rules.violation_condition: instructions or explanations that rely solely on sensory characteristics like shape, size, visual location, orientation, or sound
rules.why: Clear negative instruction corresponding to WCAG 1.3.3.

rules.quote: Expand all acronyms on their first use.
rules.violation_condition: an acronym used for the first time in a document or page without being expanded
use of double negatives within a clause or sentence
rules.why: Standard negative guidance against double negatives.

covers.quote: For most readers, aim for an average sentence length of 15 words per sentence.

examples.note: Example of varied, short sentence lengths.

parts.quote: Short sentences are great. But not always. Vary sentence length. It helps people stay engaged.

rules.quote: Long sentences should have no more than 25 words.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence containing more than 25 words
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Sentence length threshold rule, consolidating the 15-word average aim with the 25-word maximum limit.
